Alright, I've just finished the UI restyling work and captured screenshots for all the major pages: auth, home, catalog, in-game, avatar, and studio. The screenshots look good and I've reported that the catalog hats now render as real 3D thumbnails, faces work in-game, and the HUD is restyled. The next logical step is to ensure that the 3D view in the studio reflects the new camera positioning that matches the fresh visual style.

Earlier, when I was tweaking the hero block layout and adding entrance animations, I also updated the avatar preview and hat thumbnail rendering. Those changes affect how items look, but the studio's camera is still using the original default position (camPos = (20,18,20), camYaw = 0.75π, camPitch = -0.45). With the new UI elements and possibly larger or differently positioned UI overlays, the default view might be too close or at an odd angle, making the studio scene feel cramped or misaligned.

I recall that during the earlier UI overhaul, I didn't adjust the studio camera. The test suite didn't flag any issues with the studio view, but that was before the visual changes. Now that the HUD and other overlays have been restyled, I should verify that the initial camera view gives a clear perspective of the placed parts, especially since the background elements (like the new auth-bg spans) might affect perceived depth.

The best way to address this is to modify the default camera parameters in `public/js/studio/studio.js`. I want a slightly higher and farther camera to accommodate any extra UI padding and to give a more balanced view. A position of (26,20,26) should pull the camera back a bit and raise it, providing a broader view of the origin. Adjusting the yaw to `Math.PI / 4` will orient the camera to look from the +x,+z quadrant toward the origin, which aligns nicely with the typical isometric view. Slightly increasing the pitch to -0.5 (instead of -0.45) will tilt the camera down a touch more, ensuring the ground plane remains in view.

I need to make this edit precisely: replace the three lines that set `this.camPos`, `this.camYaw`, and `this.camPitch` with the new values. I won't use a global replace; just a targeted edit of that block. This should improve the studio's initial view without affecting other functionality.
